title: A 4.6μW 3.3-NEF Biopotential Amplifier with 133VPP Common-Mode Interference Tolerance and 102dB Total Common-Mode Rejection Ratio for Two-Electrode Recording System
problem: Two-electrode biopotential recording (EEG/ECG) systems experience large common-mode interference (>100V_PP) from power-source coupling via parasitic body and ground capacitances. Traditional CMI cancellation (charge-pump based) tolerates only ~20V_PP and adds noise; CM-averaging approaches ignore parasitic ground capacitance (C_GND), making them unsuitable for realistic ground-isolated systems.
motivation: Two-electrode biopotential recording is attractive for user experience and cost reduction compared to multi-electrode systems; but high CMI from 50/60Hz mains couples through parasitic impedances and must be rejected without adding noise or power overhead.
method: Novel architecture addressing C_GND parasitic capacitance: ground-isolated system with displacement current splitting between body (C_Body) and ground (C_GND). Technique maintains high input impedance (Z_IN-CM-C) while providing 102dB total CMRR and 133V_PP CMI tolerance. Low-power design achieves 4.6μW with noise efficiency factor (NEF) of 3.3, enabling precise differential biopotential measurement despite massive CM voltages.
key_novelty: High-CMRR AFE explicitly accounting for parasitic ground capacitance in ground-isolated recording, achieving 133V_PP CMI tolerance at ultra-low power with minimal noise.
contributions: 102dB total CMRR in presence of >100V_PP CMI
limitations: Abstract does not discuss gain, bandwidth, input-referred noise level, temperature drift, integration density (area), or comparison with other 2-electrode EEG/ECG systems in literature.
primary_theme: ultra-low-power high-CMRR biopotential AFE with parasitic C_GND compensation
